record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether neuron descriptions that match the most highly activating images also match broader ranges of activating images. This is a different, image-based test of the explanation-generalization issue in V6.
record.gate_note: Only Appendix A.7 bears on a claim version: it compares descriptions with images sampled from wider activation ranges. The neuron-labeling accuracy and similarity comparisons, user-rating results, and weight–concept similarity analysis do not test the listed versions. The A.7 outcomes are qualitative statements in the text; no numerical match rates are given.
record.test_reason: Appendix A.7 checks whether descriptions that fit a neuron's top activating images also fit images from wider activation ranges (top 1%, 5%). This is a vision-model, inspection-based check of V6's point that fitting the top examples overstates what is explained. No other section bears on a version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also say the result is 'somewhat expected' given sparse probe data for higher-level concepts, and that it shows the need to look beyond the top activating images. The paper's main conclusion is that CLIP-Dissect labels neurons more accurately and efficiently than prior methods.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates vision-neuron descriptions against images in activation-ranked subsets, rather than testing the original language-model audit method or its pole-level job estimates.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported description match changes with activation range: it is stronger for the top 0.1% of images and weaker for the top 1% and 5%.

fits_no_version.finding: Using a SoftWPMI cutoff, 69.7% of ResNet-18 (Places365) and 77.8% of ResNet-50 (ImageNet) neurons are called interpretable. In the human ratings, descriptions match the top-10 images for 55–80% of random neurons by layer (mean 0.655). Middle layers are hardest to describe.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Share of vision-CNN neurons with a describable function by automated labelling (vision analogue of V1, which is stated only for language models)

record.problems: The relevant A.7 findings are qualitative, with no numerical match rates or uncertainty estimates. The study evaluates only two vision networks and the pictured layers; its A.7 results are not a held-out-text or language-model test.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on the tested version were left out. Results in other sections, including neuron-labeling comparisons and user ratings, concern description-method quality rather than generalization across activation ranges.

untested.parts: Language-model neurons; held-out text; any quantitative prediction of where a neuron fires (A.7 is visual inspection of sampled images).
All: no Qwen3-32B, no pole-level job shares.
All: no language models, no dense or MoE scale comparison.
All: no InceptionV1 cat/car neuron or pose analysis.
All: no test of architecture or regularization effects on interpretable share, and no tool-driven share change.

missing.what: Low-level concepts (colours) stay consistent across top 1% and 5% images while higher-level concepts do not
Authors attribute the mismatch partly to the probe set having few images per higher-level concept; this is a confound for V6
Limitations statement: some neurons perform different functions at different activation ranges

record.verdict_notes: Only A.7 tests a version. The evidence is qualitative and covers only the most interpretable neurons in two layers, so it may understate the mismatch for typical neurons. The reader's limits_scope label based on the top-0.1% rows is removed: matching at the top range is V6's premise, not a qualification of it.

versions.untested_parts: Does not estimate the share of neuron poles with one or two jobs or unexplained poles; does not study Qwen3-32B.
Does not estimate interpretability shares across language models, dense or mixture-of-experts models, or model scales.
Does not study InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose, or recursive generalization.
Does not test architecture or regularization as causes of interpretability shares, nor the stated InceptionV1-sized model estimates.
Does not test whether attribution graphs built from a model’s own neurons explain behavior without a replacement model.
Tests visual neuron descriptions against wider ranges of activating images, not held-out text or language-model neurons; it does not test a formal prediction of where a neuron fires.
Does not automatically score explanations by simulating activations on new text or report the share of neurons meeting a score threshold.

relation.reason: Appendix A.7 reports results that bear on V6, although it is a limitation note for the authors' own method.

tranche.reason: Different method (visual inspection of activation-range samples) on the same question: whether a top-example fit predicts wider firing.

source_check.notes: A.7 is qualitative only: the most interpretable neurons of two unnamed layers. The authors call the mismatch somewhat expected given few probe images per higher-level concept. Rows that should be added: A.10 (average fit score 0.655 to the top-10 images for random neurons, 55-80% by layer), App. B (MTurk 3.57/5 vs 2.61 for random descriptions) and A.8 (69.7%/77.8% interpretable). These quantify V6's premise in the same ResNets. A.1: SoftWPMI uses only the top-100 activating images.

statements.correction: 2204.10965 A.7: most interpretable neurons of two layers (unnamed in the text) of ResNet-18 (Places365) and ResNet-50 (ImageNet); top 0.1% images match, top 1%/5% images show quite different concepts only slightly related, mainly higher-level concepts; qualitative only.
statements.problem: The 2204.10965 sentence is right. But the conditions place all the evidence at 'second-to-last or penultimate layers'. A.7 shows two layers per model and the text never names them, so penultimate is not stated for this study. Other studies' numbers were not checked.

Matches the A.7 text. The text says colours are 'more consistently represented', not that they fully stay consistent, but the meaning holds. The authors call the result 'somewhat expected' because Dprobe has few images per higher-level concept.

The 2204.10965 part is right. The text also bears on the verdict disagreement the statement reports. Appendix A.1 says SoftWPMI, used in all experiments, gives nonzero weight only to the 100 most highly activating images, so 'full-range' does not fit CLIP-Dissect's default method. Other studies' numbers were not checked.

statements.correction: 2204.10965 A.10: 50 random neurons per layer, 5 layers, ResNet-18 (Places365) and ResNet-50 (ImageNet); 2 evaluators rated fit to the 10 most highly activating images; average score 0.655, good for 55-80% of neurons by layer; evaluators agreed on 68.4%. App. B (MTurk, up to 200 random neurons per layer, 3 raters): mean 3.57/5 vs 2.61 for random descriptions. A.8: 69.7% (ResNet-18) and 77.8% (ResNet-50) of neurons above the interpretability cutoff.
statements.problem: Right that the A.7 top-0.1% match is qualitative and those rows are cannot_determine. But 'rarely measured' and 'the nearest measure is in BERT' miss that this study quantifies, for the same two ResNets, how well descriptions fit the top activating images (A.10, App. B, A.8).

The 2204.10965 part matches A.7 in substance. It drops the qualifiers that the top-1%/5% mismatch is mainly for higher-level concepts (colours stay more consistent) and that only the most interpretable neurons were shown. The low-level exception is covered in V6.against[8]. Other studies' numbers were not checked.
